newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 21.

text.p: PRAVO - Agrobanka, which has been under compulsory administration since last September, has losses of nearly nine billion crowns, according to its auditor Price Waterhouse. Because of these debts, the Czech National Bank will be forced to get rid of Agrobanka's current shareholders, and could have complications if Motoinvest, the majority shareholder, calls for the board of directors to liquidate the bank.

- While Transport Minister Martin Riman has stated that Czech Railways (CD) must reduce its losses by at least 15 percent, CD's management plans on a 30 percent reduction, according to CD's spokesman, Roman Vlasek. He estimates that this could take up to four years.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik stated in the first managers' forum yesterday that the main problems with the capital market are a low share of primary share issues, volatility of the crown, a small amount of businesses paying out dividends and a large amount of transfers outside of the organised market.

- According to the current cabinet policy, rents should increase monthly from July 1 by an average of 25 percent. Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik stated yesterday that his ministry has prepared a new concept which would double this amount.

- Since Agrobanka was placed under compulsory administration in September of last year, five foreign investors have shown interest in the company. These are Dutch ING Bank and ABN AMRO, a division of General Electric, Austrian Raiffeisen and a Korean institution whose name has yet to be announced.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Pharmacists and Vseobecna Zdravotni Pojistovna insurance company expect that from April 1, confusion could arise in pharmacies. Parliament has literally left the new health insurance law until the last minute, and health insurance companies are sceptical as to whether they will get the new list of medicines in time to prepare new prices for pharmacies by the end of March.

- The Russian munitions concern Sukhoi offered the Czech Army Su-39 fighter aircraft, and the president of the concern, Vladimir Babak, insists that in many areas, his munitions system surpasses Western aircrafts. Suchoj also offered to modernise the older types, Su-22 and Su-25, which the Czech Army already owns.
